hook: A doped polymer glows over 2000-fold brighter under stress, so afterglow maps hidden strain.
summary: Chemists found that a phosphorescent probe lights up under pressure when its singlet energy sits within 0.4 eV of the polymer's lowest triplet state. Doped polymers brightened over 2000-fold at 160 MPa, responded from about 2 MPa, and survived 500 pressure cycles. The rule is empirical, drawn from a set of probes, and tested in the lab only.
title: Molecular Mechanophores Based on Stress-Enhanced Exciton Transition between Phosphorescent Probes and Polymer Matrix
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
